hints: Integrate acceleration $a = 6t - 18$ with initial condition $v(0) = 0$ to find velocity $v(t)$.
Find the time $t > 0$ when the particle is instantaneously at rest by solving $v(t) = 0$.
Integrate $v(t)$ with $s(0) = 0$ to obtain $s(t)$, and evaluate the distance $|s(t)|$ at that time.
walkthrough:
State the relationship between acceleration and velocity:
$$v(t) = \int a(t)\,dt$$
Substitute the given acceleration $a(t) = 6t - 18$:
$$v(t) = \int (6t - 18)\,dt = 3t^2 - 18t + C$$
Because the particle starts from rest at $t = 0$, $v(0) = 0$, giving $C = 0$:
$$v(t) = 3t^2 - 18t$$

Find the instant when the particle comes to rest by setting $v(t) = 0$:
$$3t^2 - 18t = 0$$
Factor out $3t$:
$$3t(t - 6) = 0$$
Excluding the initial release at $t = 0$, the particle comes to rest at $t = 6\text{ s}$.

State the relationship between velocity and displacement:
$$s(t) = \int v(t)\,dt$$
Substitute the velocity expression:
$$s(t) = \int (3t^2 - 18t)\,dt = t^3 - 9t^2 + D$$
Since the particle starts from origin $O$ at $t = 0$, $s(0) = 0$, giving $D = 0$:
$$s(t) = t^3 - 9t^2$$

Calculate the displacement at $t = 6\text{ s}$:
$$s(6) = 6^3 - 9(6^2) = 216 - 9(36) = 216 - 324 = -108\text{ m}$$

Distance is the absolute magnitude of displacement from the starting point $O$:
$$\text{Distance} = |s(6)| = |-108| = 108\text{ m}$$
